one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled catalyst falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29: Q4 FY26 results (Aug 25), the 10-K (Sep 9) and Investor Day (Sep 17, which only reaffirmed FY27 guidance, stock -4.2%) are all behind us, and Q1 FY27 results (guided revenue $4.29-4.31B, non-GAAP EPS $2.44-2.48 incl. SBC) should come around late November, outside the window. The Oct 16 dividend ($1.38) is immaterial. What remains is AI-news headline risk (agentic tax and bookkeeping launches ahead of the 2027 filing season) and broad software-sector flows. Momentum is clearly negative: the stock was about $292 on Sep 23 and closed at $268, near its $252.84 low. Against that, at about 11.6x fully-loaded FY27 EPS a reversal bounce is plausible. I stay close to neutral: median about $266.5 (a slight downward tilt for momentum), log sd about 14.5% (50% annual vol / 3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E on FY28E EPS including SBC ($25.8 x 14x = $361, 50%) and an owner-FCF yield (FY28E FCF after SBC of about $26.5/share at 8% = $331, 50%), giving about $345 twelve months out.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28E non-GAAP EPS incl. SBC $25.8 x 14x forward P/E

inputs_detail.input: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance (now includes SBC)

inputs_detail.value: $23.94 (consensus likely mixes definitions; I use the company's guide)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 mid $23.00 x 1.12. Revenue +8-10% (Investor Day 3-yr frame: Business 10-15% CAGR, Consumer 4-8%), modest margin expansion, and about 2% net share-count reduction (FY26 repurchases $5.5B, 2% lower diluted shares, $7.9B authorization left). Trimmed below the 13-14% arithmetic to allow for TurboTax price competition.

The stock trades at 11.6x FY27 loaded EPS ($268/$23). High-single-digit revenue growth, mid-teens EPS growth and about 40% GAAP-to-FCF conversion would support a market multiple (about 18-20x), but paying-customer growth of only 3%, TurboTax units -2%, management saying price is the top churn reason, and the terminal risk from AI agents justify a steep discount. 14x is a partial re-rating, not a return to the 30x+ history.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E owner FCF (OCF - capex - SBC) about $7.1B / about 267M shares = about $26.5/share, at an 8% required yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 FCF of about $8.6B less about $2.0B SBC = $6.6B owner FCF. Grown about 4% a year (well below the 17-18% FY27 operating-income guide, because FY26 OCF looks flattered by timing) = about $7.1B, on about 267M shares.
An 8% yield on SBC-burdened FCF means about 4% growth with a 12% cost of equity. That prices real terminal-value risk from AI disruption on top of about a 9-10% equity cost for a mature franchise.

bear.story: AI-native filers and price cuts erode TurboTax in the 2027 season (units fall again, the ARPC cut goes deeper), Consumer revenue misses the 4-6% guide, QBO customer growth stays about flat and pricing power fades. FY28 EPS is flat around $23, and the multiple compresses to about 8.5-9x as the market treats Intuit as a melting ice cube.

base.story: FY27 guide is roughly met (revenue +9-10%, EPS about $23), and the 2027 tax season is stable with units about flat and TurboTax Live still growing. Buybacks continue at about $5B+ a year and the multiple edges up to about 12-13x FY28 EPS of about $25.

bull.story: The AI-native TurboTax season wins back share, Big Bets (assisted tax, money, mid-market IES) keep growing about 30%, and the AI narrative flips to Intuit as a data and distribution winner. The multiple re-rates to about 16-17x FY28 EPS of about $26, toward the sell-side median target of about $405-421.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $190 the stock would trade at about 8x FY27 fully-loaded EPS and about a 13% owner-FCF yield. That only makes sense if earnings are expected to shrink, most likely because the 2027 tax season shows accelerating TurboTax unit losses or ARPC collapse, or because QBO subscriber counts turn negative. At that point the franchise-durability thesis (business platform 10-15% CAGR, consumer 4-8%) would be broken, not just de-rated.

key_uncertainties: Whether AI agents structurally compress DIY tax pricing (management already concedes price is the top churn reason and is 'deliberately accepting lower initial DIY tax ARPC')
QuickBooks Online customer growth: FY26 growth was driven by price and mix, with online paying customers up only 3%
Quality of FY26 operating cash flow ($8.8B vs $6.2B in FY25) and how much of it recurs
Credit Karma cyclicality (personal loans, cards) in a consumer-credit slowdown
Whether a momentum-driven de-rating keeps going regardless of fundamentals (stock -62% over 1 year, near its lows)
reasoning: Primary documents show a business still growing, with growth slowing. FY26 revenue was $21.4B (+14%), non-GAAP EPS $24.27 (old definition), OCF $8.8B, and buybacks $5.5B cut diluted shares 2%. The FY27 guide is revenue +9-10% with TurboTax +2-3%, Mailchimp flat and Credit Karma +11-13%, and non-GAAP EPS of $22.88-23.12 now fully burdened by about $2.0B SBC. The 10-K discloses online paying customers +3%, US TurboTax units -2% (39.0M), a restructuring plan announced in May 2026 and 267.2M shares outstanding. At $268, INTU is about 11.6x loaded FY27 EPS and about a 9% SBC-burdened FCF yield ($71.6B market cap, net debt about $0.5B). That is very cheap unless earnings are about to decline. The market is clearly pricing that risk (agentic-AI disruption of tax and bookkeeping, and management conceding price-driven churn), and momentum is poor (from $292 on Sep 23 to $268, near the $252.84 low). I value it at about $345 (P/E and owner-FCF methods), but I don't assume full convergence within 12 months, because the decisive evidence (the 2027 tax season) lands only in Apr-May 2027. My scenario mix is bear $200 (33%), base $310 (44%) and bull $430 (23%), each with about 20-25% dispersion. That gives a median of about $295-300, P(>=$268) of about 0.60, and a fat left tail, consistent with the 50% realized vol. The sell-side median target (about $405-421) sits above my base, and I treat it as lagging. Research was limited: I could not text-parse the Q4 call script or the Investor Day PDF, so I relied on the 8-K and 10-K plus press accounts of the Investor Day, and Twelve Data analyst endpoints were unavailable on the current plan.
